- Dark grayish-green coloration overall
- Necrosis spreading from edges inward
- No obvious target rings or powdery coating

Top candidates: Late Blight, Bacterial Canker, Early Blight, Septoria. Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with the most likely.

Early Blight shows widespread yellowing/browning - not a close match. Let me check Septoria Leaf Blotch.
Microscopic image. Let me check remaining classes - Bacterial Speck, Anthracnose, Southern Blight, and Cucumber Mosaic Virus.

| Class | Reference visual | Match to test? |
|-------|-----------------|----------------|

| Late_Blight | Grayish water-soaked patches (macro); microscopic (others) | Weak |

| Early_Blight | Widespread whole-plant browning | Different |

| Others | Microscopic, fruit rot, ooze tests, distortion | Not applicable |

**Test image:** Single tomato leaf on gray surface with brown apical (tip) necrosis and marginal scorch extending inward, dark green remaining tissue, no spots or powdery coating.

**Best match:** Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato (Bugwood_1.jpg) — that reference showed nearly identical brown, dried marginal necrosis on leaves with green centers remaining, which is the classic marginal scorch symptom of bacterial canker.
